the serum levels of albumine, prealbumine, vitamin D and zinc were reduced and the serum levels of TNF-α, IL-6, LPL and CRP were elevated in the patients with NCSCLC.
the serum levels of IL6, IL1β, TNFa, CRP, LPL, albumin, prealbuim, Zn, vitamin-D, and GPS were reduced in patients with NSLC that completed the treatment and had increased survival.

the serum levels of inflammatory markers, IL-6, TNF- α, IL-1b and CRP, and also the serum levels of nutritional markers, albumin, pre-albumin, vitamin D and Zn, are significantly associated with chemotherapy outcomes and survival of the patients with aNSLC undergoing adjuvant treatment.

a new approach to determine the prognostic nutritional markers in the patients with NSCLCs.
the evaluation of the nutritional and inflammatory markers as a prognostic indicator of the chemotherapy outcomes and survival.
the evaluation of the nutritional and inflammatory status in aNSCLC.

malnutrition and cachectic patients with advanced NSCLC may have poor response to the treatment and poor survival.
malnutrition and cachectic patients with aNSLC have a poor prognosis, and the nutritional and inflammatory markers can be used to predict the chemotherapy outcomes in these patients.

serum levels of IL6, IL-β, TNF-a, CRP, LPL, and GPS can predict chemotherapy outcomes in patients with a NSCLC.
